blocks.text: Quantifiers help us write general rules about the library. For example, ∀x, Student(x) → Borrows(x, Book) means “every student borrows a book.” ∃y, Book(y) ∧ Available(y) means “there exists at least one book that is available.” These statements help define rules and conditions in a precise way. Quantifiers allow us to describe both general situations and specific cases in the library system.

blocks.title: Class Activity
blocks.text: Ask students to write rules like “All students must attend class” using universal quantifiers.
